questions.text_english:
(1) The term Artificial Intelligence spells a future in which this emerging technology will impact every aspect of human existence. In fact, little do we know, it has already crept into our lives, slowly, but surely. Look around you education, health care, industry, innovation, robots, robotic surgeries, transportation, home service it's already there. It will change the lifestyle of everyone from the technology industry to normal people.

(2) The past fifteen years have seen considerable AI advances in education. You enter school and AI takes your attendance using face recognition. Various applications are in wide use by educators and learners today. AI technologies assist teachers in the classroom. Learning at home is likely to expand significantly, along with learning based on virtual reality applications. Though quality education will always require active engagement by human teachers, AI promises to enhance education at all levels, especially by providing personalization at scale.

(3) The evolution of new technologies, mobile, and the Internet are changing lifestyles. Artificial intelligence is playing an important role in every sector such as banking, driving, education, e-commerce, electronics, robotics. Systems of artificial intelligence are aiming to stimulate execution and decision-making that is human-like. In targeted applications, substantial increases in the future uses of AI technologies, including more driverless cars, healthcare diagnostics and targeted treatments, and physical assistance for elder care can be expected. AI and robotics will also be applied across the globe in industries struggling such as agriculture, food processing and factories. They will facilitate delivery of online purchases through flying drones, self-driving trucks or robots.

(4) AI-based applications could improve health outcomes and quality of life for millions of people in the coming years - prime applications include clinical decision support, patient monitoring and coaching, automated devices to assist in surgery or patient care, and management of healthcare systems. Recent successes, such as mining social media to infer possible health risks, machine learning to predict patients at risk, and robotics to support surgery have expanded a sense of possibility for AI in healthcare.

(5) People's future relationships with machines will become ever more personalized as AI systems learn to adapt to individual personalities, ambitions and goals. These AI applications will help monitor people's well-being, alert them to the impending risks, and deliver services when needed or wanted.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage:

sub_questions.text_english: Select the word that most appropriately defines Artificial Intelligence today.
sub_questions.solution: The passage highlights that AI is already present in numerous aspects of life including education, healthcare, industry, and home services, making it pervasive or universal rather than just rewarding, luxurious, or temporary.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the connection between 'face recognition' in school education and AI?

key_points: Face recognition is an application of AI technology used to automate attendance in schools.

sub_questions.solution: Face recognition is an AI-driven technology that is currently being used in school settings to automate the process of taking student attendance.

sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following do you infer from para 2?

options_english.A: School education will become a virtual engagement.
options_english.B: The teacher will be replaced by AI.
options_english.C: Human teachers will play a passive role in the classroom.

sub_questions.solution: Paragraph 2 explicitly states that while AI promises to enhance education, quality education will always require the active engagement of human teachers, implying they remain irreplaceable.

sub_questions.text_english: Share evidence from the text, in about 40 words, about how AI can support the field of education.

key_points: AI assists teachers in classrooms.
It enables learning at home through virtual reality.
It provides personalization at scale for students.

sub_questions.solution: According to the passage, AI supports education by assisting teachers in the classroom and enabling learning at home through virtual reality applications. Furthermore, it significantly enhances education at all levels by providing personalization at scale to meet individual student needs.

sub_questions.text_english: The phrase 'stimulate execution' in para 3 nearly means:
sub_questions.solution: In the context of AI systems aiming to perform tasks like a human, 'stimulate execution' refers to driving or motivating the implementation of actions and decisions.

sub_questions.text_english: With evidence from the text, explain in about 40 words, two ways in which AI will help in the healthcare sector.

key_points: AI improves health outcomes through clinical decision support and patient monitoring.
AI assists in surgeries through automated devices and robotics.

sub_questions.solution: AI helps the healthcare sector by providing clinical decision support, patient monitoring, and coaching to improve outcomes. Additionally, it uses robotics and automated devices to assist surgeons during procedures, expanding the possibilities for safer and more precise medical care.

sub_questions.text_english: According to the passage, why does the author conclude that people's relationships with machines will become more personalised?

key_points: AI systems can learn to adapt to individual personalities.
They can align with human ambitions and goals.

sub_questions.solution: The author concludes this because AI systems are evolving to learn and adapt to individual human personalities, ambitions, and goals. By understanding these unique traits, the machines can better monitor well-being and provide services tailored to what people need or want.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following statement: AI will make the commercial supply chain smoother by _______

fill_values: facilitating the delivery of online purchases through flying drones, self-driving trucks or robots

sub_questions.solution: AI will make the commercial supply chain smoother by facilitating the delivery of online purchases through autonomous means like flying drones, self-driving trucks, or robots as mentioned in paragraph 3.

sub_questions.text_english: Read the five headlines and identify the option that displays the headline/s that do/do not correspond with occurrences in the passage.
sub_questions.solution: Headline IV (rising unemployment) and Headline V (factory owners fearing unpredictability) are not supported by the passage, which focuses on the benefits and integration of AI across sectors.

questions.text_english:
(1) A recent survey conducted by an independent research firm sought to measure levels of happiness among youth aged 16-24 years in seven countries. The findings revealed some intriguing insights into what makes today's youth happiest, as well as which factors influence their overall well-being. In India, an overwhelming majority of the youth reported feeling satisfied with their lives, with 87% rating of their overall happiness as 'high' or 'very high.' Financial security was identified as the primary source of happiness for 66%, followed by family support (89%), having a purpose in life (50%), and work or studies (40%). Unfortunately, 65% reported feeling stress related to academic performance or workload, while 25% reported feeling lonely. These figures point to a need for increased mental health support among India's youth.

(2) These surveys also revealed that family support is an important source of contentment for young people across countries. In Europe, 59% of respondents said that their families were a major source of happiness; in France this figure was 67%, and 63% in Germany. In North America, 64% rated family as an important factor for well-being in Canada, while 61% did so in the United States. Similarly, 89% of survey respondents in India named family support as a major contributor to their overall contentment level.

(3) It is clear that stress has a significant impact on the happiness of today's youth. The findings suggest that young people need better resources to manage their mental health and well-being. This may include access to counselling services, mindfulness activities and support groups to help them cope with challenging circumstances. It is also important to provide financial support so as to reduce some of the economic pressures.

(4) In India, 65% of youth surveyed reported feeling anxious about their academic performance or workload, while 25% felt lonely. These figures are especially significant given how important family support is for young people's overall contentment.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage:

sub_questions.text_english: What are the two findings that the survey mentioned in paragraph 1 reveals? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: 87% of Indian youth rate their happiness as high or very high.
Factors like financial security, family support, purpose, and work/studies influence their well-being.

sub_questions.solution: The survey reveals that an overwhelming majority of Indian youth, specifically 87%, feel satisfied with their lives, rating their happiness as high or very high. Additionally, it identifies key factors influencing their well-being, such as financial security, family support, purpose, and work or studies.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in about 40 words the statement It is also important to provide financial support so as to reduce some of the economic pressures.

key_points: Financial security is a primary source of happiness for 66% of Indian youth.
Reducing economic pressure helps alleviate stress and improves mental well-being.

sub_questions.solution: Since financial security is the primary source of happiness for 66% of the surveyed youth, providing financial support is crucial. Addressing economic pressures directly helps reduce stress, thereby enabling young people to manage their mental health and overall well-being more effectively.

sub_questions.text_english: Elaborate giving data, the statement Stress has a significant impact on the happiness of today's youth.

key_points: 65% of Indian youth report stress from academic workload, and 25% report feeling lonely.

sub_questions.solution: The impact of stress is evident in the survey data, which shows that 65% of Indian youth feel anxious due to academic performance or workload, while 25% report experiencing feelings of loneliness.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following factors does not play a substantial role in the well-being of Indian youth?
sub_questions.solution: The passage identifies family support, financial security (economic stability), and social factors (like loneliness) as significant, but it does not mention books and literature as a primary factor.

sub_questions.text_english: State whether True or False: It is not necessary to provide financial support to the youth as only academic performance plays an upper hand in deciding the stress level.
sub_questions.solution: This statement is false because the passage explicitly states that financial security is the primary source of happiness for 66% of youth and recommends providing financial support to reduce economic pressures.

sub_questions.text_english: What are the top choices which are of maximum value to today's youth?
sub_questions.solution: The passage emphasizes the high value youth place on collectivism (implied by social satisfaction) and family ties (89% citing it as a major contributor to contentment).

sub_questions.text_english: The mental health of today's youth can be managed by resources like _______ and _______
sub_questions.solution: The passage suggests that resources such as counselling services, mindfulness activities, and support groups are essential for managing mental health.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the following sources that provide happiness to today's youth in descending order: (a) purposefulness (b) family support (c) financial status (d) stress

key_points: Family support (89%), Financial status (66%), Purposefulness (50%)

sub_questions.solution: The descending order of happiness sources is: family support (89%), financial status (66%), and purposefulness (50%). Note that stress is a negative factor, not a source of happiness.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the two, (a) or (b), in about 50 words.

sub_questions.text_english: To encourage students to participate in outdoor activities, your school has planned a 7-day trek to Rohtang Pass for students of classes VIII - X during the summer vacation. Write a notice for the school notice board giving all the necessary information. You are Raghav/Ragini, Secretary Trekking Club, Amar Bahadur School.

key_points: Format: Notice heading, date, title, details (what, when, who, fee, deadline), contact name.

sub_questions.solution: AMAR BAHADUR SCHOOL, NOTICE. June 5, 2026. TREK TO ROHTANG PASS. This is to inform students of classes VIII-X that the Trekking Club is organizing a 7-day trek to Rohtang Pass during summer vacation. Interested students should submit their names and a fee of Rs. 2000 to the undersigned by June 15, 2026. Raghav, Secretary, Trekking Club.

sub_questions.text_english: The problem of the residents' parking of vehicles has become a source of growing concern. As Secretary of Goodwill Flats Welfare Association, Shripur, write a notice informing the residents about a meeting to discuss the problem and find an acceptable solution.

key_points: Format: Notice heading, date, meeting details, purpose.

sub_questions.solution: GOODWILL FLATS WELFARE ASSOCIATION, SHRIPUR. NOTICE. June 5, 2026. MEETING REGARDING PARKING ISSUES. All residents are requested to attend an urgent meeting on June 10, 2026, at 5 PM in the Community Hall to discuss the rising concerns regarding vehicle parking and to find a collective, acceptable solution. Secretary, Welfare Association.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the two, (a) or (b), in about 50 words.

sub_questions.text_english: You are the Student Head, Cultural Affairs Club at Newton Public School. The school is holding its annual function on Saturday, April 20th, 2024 at 11 am. The Honourable Education Minister, Dr. Shah has consented to be the Chief Guest. Design an invitation card to be sent to the parents and other invitees.
sub_questions.solution: The Principal, Staff and Students of Newton Public School cordially invite you to the Annual Function on Saturday, April 20, 2024, at 11:00 am in the School Auditorium. Dr. Shah, Honourable Education Minister, has kindly consented to be the Chief Guest. Please join us for this celebration. RSVP: Cultural Affairs Club.

sub_questions.text_english: You are a renowned doctor and have been invited by your school alumni as Chief Guest to the Annual Graduation Ceremony of Green School on Sunday, March 24th, 2024. Write a letter to the President of the Alumni Association expressing your inability to attend due to a prior commitment.
sub_questions.solution: Dear President, Thank you for inviting me as the Chief Guest for the Annual Graduation Ceremony at Green School. Unfortunately, I am unable to attend due to a prior professional commitment. Please convey my heartiest congratulations to the graduating students and wish them great success in their future endeavors.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the two, (a) or (b), in 120-150 words.

sub_questions.text_english: You are Amar/Anita, a fresh MBA graduate. Write a letter to India Helptel Company along with your bio-data, expressing your interest in the position of Management Trainee advertised.
sub_questions.solution: 12, Model Town, Khushbagh. June 5, 2026. The HR Manager, India Helptel Company. Subject: Application for the post of Management Trainee. Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to express my strong interest in the Management Trainee position advertised in the newspaper. As a fresh MBA graduate with a specialization in Marketing from Singla Institute of Management, I possess excellent communication skills and proficiency in English and the state language. I am a dedicated professional eager to contribute to your logistics department. My enclosed bio-data provides further details about my qualifications. I look forward to the possibility of an interview to discuss how my skills align with your company's requirements. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely, Amar/Anita.

sub_questions.text_english: An increase in the number of vehicles on the road has increased instances of traffic snarls, road rage and accidents. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily showing your concern and examining the reasons for such behaviour. Provide suggestions.
sub_questions.solution: To the Editor, National Daily. Subject: Concerns over rising traffic incidents. Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the increasing traffic snarls, road rage, and accidents. The surge in the number of vehicles, particularly multiple cars per family and the rise of budgeted cab services, has overwhelmed our roads. Many drivers fail to adhere to basic traffic rules, which worsens the situation. To manage this, authorities must improve traffic management during peak hours and implement laws more strictly. Furthermore, the media should play a proactive role in creating awareness about road safety and responsible driving. It is high time we address these issues to ensure our roads are safe for everyone. I hope this letter prompts a necessary discussion on this pressing concern. Yours truly, Brinda/Bharat.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the two, (a) or (b), in 120-150 words.

sub_questions.text_english: Write an article on 'India as a popular choice of Foreign Visitors'. You are Leela/Laksh.
sub_questions.solution: India as a Popular Choice for Foreign Visitors. By Leela/Laksh. India is rapidly emerging as a premier global tourist destination. This influx of foreign visitors is a significant boost to our economy, as it generates numerous jobs for the local population and promotes our rich culture, traditional food, and unique handicrafts. Whether it is medical tourism, religious pilgrimage, or ecotourism, India’s diversity places it prominently on the world map. However, we must continue to strengthen the efforts of authorities to maintain these standards. The role of media in creating positive awareness is vital. Furthermore, we must establish information centres for all tourists to ensure their experience is seamless and welcoming. With concerted efforts, India can continue to be a top destination for travelers worldwide.

sub_questions.text_english: The senior residents of your colony have initiated a Reading Club for the children of a neighbourhood slum. As Ramesh/Ranjita, the local correspondent, write a report covering the project.
sub_questions.solution: Report: Senior Citizens’ Initiative for Slum Children. By Ramesh/Ranjita. Our colony's senior residents have taken a commendable initiative by launching a Reading Club for children from the neighbouring slum. Every Sunday morning, these volunteers dedicate two hours to this noble cause. The primary goal is to support the children with their school texts and improve their literacy skills. The sessions include comprehension quizzing and newspaper reading, which not only builds their vocabulary but also encourages healthy discussions on current affairs. This project has been a beacon of hope, empowering underprivileged children with the habit of reading and critical thinking. The initiative has received widespread appreciation from the community, as it bridges the educational gap while fostering a sense of social responsibility among the elderly.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).

sub_questions.text_english: (a) A thing of beauty is a joy forever. Its loveliness increases, it will never pass into nothingness; but will keep A bower quiet for us, and a sleep Full of sweet dreams, and health, and quiet breathing.
Which of the following themes is best represented in the given extract?

options_english.B: Beauty lies in possession of expensive things.
options_english.C: Beauty is synonymous with power and riches.
options_english.D: Beauty lies in our rich heritage and palaces and temples.

sub_questions.solution: The extract emphasizes that beauty provides a 'quiet bower' and 'sweet dreams', signifying peace and mental security.

sub_questions.text_english: A thing of beauty never passes into nothingness because it is _______
sub_questions.solution: A thing of beauty never passes into nothingness because its loveliness increases and it is eternal.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Quiet bower' means a pleasant, shady, quiet place under trees or in the woods. This creates a sense of _______

key_points: Peace and tranquility.

sub_questions.solution: It creates a sense of deep peace and tranquility, providing an escape from the worries of the world.

sub_questions.text_english: State whether the given statement is True or False: The quality of a thing ensures that its beauty lasts forever.
sub_questions.solution: The poem states that a thing of beauty increases in loveliness and never passes into nothingness, validating the statement.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the rhyme scheme in lines 3 and 4, which word will rhyme with them?
sub_questions.solution: Lines 3 and 4 end with 'keep' and 'sleep'. 'Sweep' rhymes with these words.

sub_questions.text_english: The use of the word 'health' in the extract suggests that beautiful things will give us a happier and more wholesome life. It creates a powerful image of _______
sub_questions.solution: The mention of 'health' and 'sweet dreams' creates an image of mental and physical rejuvenation.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Aunt Jennifer's tigers prance across a screen, Bright topaz denizens of a world of green. They do not fear the men beneath the tree; They pace in sleek chivalric certainty.
Which of the following are symbolised by the 'tigers'?
sub_questions.solution: The tigers symbolize the feminine world, bold/fearless creatures, and the world of beautiful handicrafts, contrasting with the masculine world.

sub_questions.text_english: State whether True or False: The creator of the tigers was fearless and assertive like the tigers.
sub_questions.solution: Aunt Jennifer is depicted as timid and oppressed; her fearlessness is only expressed through her art, not her personality.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following sentence: The use of the word 'topaz' suggests that the image of the tiger on the screen is _______
sub_questions.solution: The word 'topaz' suggests that the tigers appear as bright, golden, and radiant creatures against the green background.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Tigers do not fear the men beneath the tree' because they are _______
sub_questions.solution: The tigers do not fear the men because they represent pure, bold, and fearless creatures.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the poem's rhyme scheme in lines 1 and 2, which of the following will rhyme?
sub_questions.solution: Lines 1 and 2 end with 'screen' and 'green'. Words like 'mean' and 'cream' rhyme with these.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Chivalric certainty' refers to which poetic device?
sub_questions.solution: The repetition of the 'c' sound in 'chivalric certainty' is an example of alliteration.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).

sub_questions.text_english: Derry: I....there....I thought this was an empty place. I didn't know there was anybody here.... Mr. Lamb: That's all right. I'm here. What are you afraid of, boy? That's all right. Derry: I thought it was empty....an empty house. Mr. Lamb: So it is. Since I'm out here in the garden. It is empty. Until I go back inside. In the meantime, I'm out here and likely to stop. A day like this. Beautiful day. Not a day to be indoors. Derry: [Panic] I've got to go.
Derry was stammering because of:
sub_questions.solution: Derry is startled by finding Mr. Lamb in the garden, and his panic-induced stammering stems from fear of human interaction.

sub_questions.text_english: Derry insisted on going back because _______

fill_values: he was uncomfortable in the presence of a stranger

sub_questions.solution: Derry insisted on leaving because he was extremely uncomfortable and anxious around people, as shown by his panic.

sub_questions.text_english: Mr. Lamb was trying to tell Derry that:

options_english.A: it was a matter of perception.
options_english.C: he spent all his days in the garden.

sub_questions.solution: Mr. Lamb suggests that the house being 'empty' or not depends on whether he is inside or in the garden, highlighting his philosophical approach to perception.

sub_questions.text_english: From the extract, one can infer that Mr. Lamb was a/an:
sub_questions.solution: Mr. Lamb’s gentle and welcoming tone towards the panicked, scared boy shows he is a compassionate and understanding person.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Anyway, here's what happened at Grand Central. One night last summer I worked late at the office. I was in a hurry to get uptown to my apartment so I decided to take the subway from Grand Central because it's faster than the bus. Now, I don't know why this should have happened to me. I'm just an ordinary guy named Charley, thirty-one years old, and I was wearing a tan gabardine suit and a straw hat with a fancy band; I passed a dozen men who looked just like me.
List any two details about how Charley was dressed up.

key_points: Tan gabardine suit
Straw hat with a fancy band

sub_questions.solution: Charley was wearing a tan gabardine suit and a straw hat with a fancy band.

sub_questions.text_english: Charley decided to use the subway because it was :
sub_questions.solution: Charley explicitly states he chose the subway because it was faster than the bus.

sub_questions.text_english: Landing at the third level was due to Charley's flight of _______
sub_questions.solution: Landing at the third level is a result of Charley's flight of imagination, as he attempts to escape the pressures of modern life.

sub_questions.text_english: Which time frame is represented through the kind of outfit mentioned in the extract?
sub_questions.solution: The attire described, particularly the gabardine suit and straw hat, is characteristic of the fashion in the pre-World War era.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).

sub_questions.text_english: (a) They have lived here for more than thirty years without an identity, without permits but with ration cards that get their names on voters' lists and enable them to buy grain. Food is more important for survival than identity. If at the end of the day we can feed our families and go to bed without an aching stomach, we would rather live here than in the fields that gave us no grain,say a group of women in tattered saris when I asked them why they left their beautiful land of green fields and rivers. Wherever they find food, they pitch their tents.
The ragpickers have been living there for _______ decades.
sub_questions.solution: The extract states that they have lived there for more than thirty years, which is three decades.

sub_questions.text_english: Why do these people have ration cards?

key_points: To get their names on voter lists and buy grain.

sub_questions.solution: They have ration cards to get their names on the voter lists, which enables them to buy grain for their survival.

sub_questions.text_english: What do you infer about their lifestyle from the phrase 'pitch their tents'?

key_points: Nomadic and unstable lifestyle.

sub_questions.solution: The phrase implies a nomadic, unstable, and insecure lifestyle where they must keep moving in search of food.

sub_questions.text_english: In spite of the hardships, they are not willing to go back to their homeland because _______

key_points: They get food for survival here, which they couldn't get in their homeland.

sub_questions.solution: They are not willing to return because their homeland could not provide enough grain to feed them, whereas here they can at least survive.

sub_questions.text_english: The women had a/an _______ approach towards life.
sub_questions.solution: The women’s focus on survival and feeding their families shows a pragmatic, or practical, approach to their dire circumstances.

sub_questions.text_english: What does the term 'go to bed without an aching stomach' indicate?

key_points: Having enough food to eat.

sub_questions.solution: The term indicates the basic necessity of having enough food to satisfy their hunger at the end of the day.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) Their spontaneous demonstration, in thousands, around the courthouse was the beginning of their liberation from fear of the British. The officials felt powerless without Gandhi's cooperation. He helped them regulate the crowd. He was polite and friendly. He was giving them concrete proof that their might, hitherto dreaded and unquestioned, could be challenged by Indians. The government was baffled. The prosecutor requested the judge to postpone the trial. Apparently, the authorities wished to consult their superiors.
The result of the demonstration was that _______

key_points: It marked the beginning of their liberation from fear of the British.

sub_questions.solution: The demonstration marked the beginning of the people's liberation from the fear of British authority.

sub_questions.text_english: The participants of the spontaneous demonstration were :
sub_questions.solution: The thousands of people surrounding the courthouse were the peasants and ordinary people of Champaran supporting Gandhi.

sub_questions.text_english: Gandhi cooperated with the British by :

options_english.B: remaining quiet when he was accused.
options_english.C: helping to manage the mob of people.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhi showed his non-violent approach by helping the British officials regulate the large, unmanageable crowd.

sub_questions.text_english: The statement 'Apparently, the authorities wished to consult their superiors' was indicative of the Britisher's _______

key_points: Inability to handle the situation independently.

sub_questions.solution: It indicates that the British authorities were confused and lacked the autonomy to handle Gandhi's challenge effectively without higher-level instructions.

sub_questions.text_english: With reference to the extract, the word 'baffled' most nearly means:
sub_questions.solution: The government was 'baffled' because they were confused by Gandhi’s tactics and the massive public support for him.

sub_questions.text_english: Whose 'might' did this demonstration question?

key_points: The might of the British empire.

sub_questions.solution: The demonstration challenged the unchecked might and authority of the British colonial government.

questions.text: Answer any five of the following six questions in 40-50 words each.

sub_questions.text_english: What inference can you draw about Sophie's relationship with her father from the story 'Going Places'?
sub_questions.solution: Sophie's relationship with her father is strained and characterized by a lack of emotional connection. Her father is portrayed as pragmatic, unsympathetic, and dismissive of her dreams. He finds her fantasies and stories tiresome, leading to a palpable distance between them that Sophie struggles to bridge.

sub_questions.text_english: We miss a thing when we are in fear of losing it. Substantiate this statement with two examples from 'The Last Lesson'.
sub_questions.solution: In 'The Last Lesson', the villagers realize the value of their language only when they are about to lose it due to the new order from Berlin. First, the elderly villagers sitting in the classroom signify their regret for not attending school earlier. Second, Franz feels a sudden love for his books and language, recognizing them as old friends he can no longer bear to lose.

sub_questions.text_english: What did the peddler say in his defence when it was clear that he was not the person the ironmaster thought him to be?
sub_questions.solution: When confronted, the peddler maintained that he had never claimed to be the Captain. He explained that he had tried to leave the forge and had been brought there against his will. He emphasized that no harm had been done and that he was willing to put on his rags again, showing he was not a thief.

sub_questions.text_english: What does 'The God That Failed' refer to?
sub_questions.solution: In 'Poets and Pancakes', 'The God That Failed' refers to a collection of six essays by famous writers who described their disillusionment with communism. It highlights their initial belief in a utopian ideology that ultimately disappointed them, serving as a metaphor for the fading of their idealism.

sub_questions.text_english: What according to Umberto Eco is the belief that most journalists and publishers have?
sub_questions.solution: Umberto Eco notes that journalists and publishers often believe that people, especially children, are interested in 'trashy' and 'over-simplified' content. He argues that they underestimate the public's intelligence, whereas he himself believes that people are capable of and interested in serious, complex scholarly topics.

sub_questions.text_english: It is said that the 'Face is a mirror of one's emotions.' Why did the poet 'smile and smile'?
sub_questions.solution: The poet smiles and smiles in 'My Mother at Sixty-six' to hide her inner pain and anxiety from her aging mother. This forced smile serves as a mask to reassure both herself and her mother, ensuring that the final farewell is not marred by the visible signs of her fear and emotional turmoil.

questions.text: Answer any two of the following three questions in 40-50 words each.

sub_questions.text_english: What confusion does the Dewan have when the Tiger King broaches the topic of his marriage?
sub_questions.solution: When the King asks the Dewan to find him a royal bride from a state with a large tiger population, the Dewan becomes confused. He believes the King might be thinking of marrying a tiger, not a princess, and tells him that he already has a tiger (his wife) and he does not need another one.

sub_questions.text_english: My Antarctic experience was full of such epiphanies,says Tishani Doshi. Which experience does she consider the best and why?
sub_questions.solution: Tishani Doshi considers the experience of standing on the ice shelf at Antarctica as the best. She describes it as an epiphany because being in that pristine, vast white landscape made her acutely aware of the fragility of the Earth and the impact of human history on climate change, fostering a deeper environmental consciousness.

sub_questions.text_english: Zitkala-Sa says, Eating by formula wasn't the hardest trial in that first day.What does she mean by 'Eating by formula'?
sub_questions.solution: By 'eating by formula,' Zitkala-Sa refers to the rigid, rule-bound way of dining at her boarding school. The children had to follow specific, synchronized instructions for every action—waiting for the bell to sit, scrape chairs, and begin eating. This lack of spontaneity made her feel suppressed and dehumanized.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words.

sub_questions.text_english: Imagine you are John Keats. What advice might you offer to Robert Frost in the context of his 'The sadness that lurks near the open window'? Pen down your advice in a letter.
sub_questions.solution: Dear Robert, I have recently read your poem 'A Roadside Stand' and felt the deep sadness that lurks near that open window, longing for the city money that never comes. While I understand the pain of unfulfilled hope and the stark contrast between the rural simplicity and the city’s indifference, I urge you to look beyond the immediate suffering. Even in a world filled with sorrow, beauty remains a constant source of strength. Whether it is the shade of the trees or the simple rhythms of life, these eternal things provide us with the endurance needed to face life's harshest realities. Despite the fact that our lives are full of sorrow and suffering, the beautiful things around us give us the strength to endure the sadness of life. Do not let despair dim your vision. Warmly, John Keats.

sub_questions.text_english: Create a comprehensive comparison of the themes present in 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers' and 'My Mother at Sixty-six'. Specifically discuss the different ways each poem addresses the concept of struggle and resilience.
sub_questions.solution: Both 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers' and 'My Mother at Sixty-six' explore themes of human fragility, internal struggle, and the passage of time. Aunt Jennifer struggles with systemic oppression and a stifling marriage, finding resilience only through her art, where she creates brave tigers that symbolize the spirit she cannot embody in her own life. Her struggle is externalized and permanent, confined to her embroidery. In contrast, Kamala Das’s poem captures the internal struggle of watching a parent age and facing the inevitable reality of death. Her resilience is reflected in her attempt to mask this anxiety with a smile, seeking comfort in her own mental strength and acceptance of life's cycles. While Jennifer retreats into art to survive her pain, Das faces her fear directly but chooses to compartmentalize it to protect her mother’s peace.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 120-150 words.

sub_questions.text_english: Dr. Sadao is disturbed and in a dilemma since he has decided to help the enemy soldier. Describe his conflict and the challenges faced in the form of a diary entry.
sub_questions.solution: June 5, 2026. Today has been a day of immense turmoil. I have made the decision to save the American soldier, yet I am plagued by doubt. Am I a traitor to my country, or am I adhering to the sacred oath of a physician? My professional duty to save a life clashes with my loyalty to Japan during this war. The presence of the soldier in my house has alienated my servants and terrified my wife, Hana. I feel a heavy burden, as every passing moment is a gamble with our safety. I am constantly watching for any sign of betrayal or discovery. I am a surgeon first, but the weight of this moral conflict is breaking me. I pray that my conscience and my duty reach an understanding, for I am truly at a crossroad.

sub_questions.text_english: In the story 'The Third Level', reality and fantasy are interwoven. Justify.
sub_questions.solution: In 'The Third Level', Jack Finney masterfully weaves reality and fantasy to highlight the protagonist's desire to escape modern anxieties. The reality is Charley's mundane life in 1950s New York—full of stress, fast-paced work, and dissatisfaction. The fantasy begins when he discovers a 'third level' at Grand Central Station, which acts as a gateway to the peaceful, pre-war world of 1894. The author grounds the fantasy in realistic details, such as the authentic architectural style of the station, the newspaper he finds, and the specific attire of the commuters, making the reader question if the third level is a genuine discovery or merely a subconscious projection. This blurring of lines underscores the theme that when the present becomes unbearable, the human mind inevitably seeks refuge in an idealized, nostalgic past, making the 'Third Level' a sanctuary born of sheer desperation.
